conviction_note: Findings sum to roughly +1.7 points (AI monetisation plumbing +1.5, buyback float shrinkage +1.0, monday.com seat/retention read-through +1.0, offset by finance-leadership churn -1.0 and a stock trading above the sell-side average target after a technical run-up -0.8); nudged to +2.0 because the company's own 7-print base rate is 5 up with a +3.9% mean, but held far inside the 14.4% implied move because nothing I found is large enough to justify more than a modest tilt against a +6.6 skew.

findings.finding: Asana's live production API now licenses AI Studio as a per-user seat with three tiers - ai_studio_plus, ai_studio_pro and ai_studio_max - of which 'Max' appears nowhere on Asana's public pricing page or help docs, and every AI run is tagged with a credit_source of 'paid' or 'free'; this is the recurring, seat-priced AI line management pre-committed on the Q1 call to quantify for the first time on THIS call.
findings.source_date: 2026-09-03 (retrieved; the endpoint was announced 2026-07-02 per Asana's changelog)
findings.why_not_priced: Sell-side coverage is 15 analysts with only 2 published quarterly estimates, and every preview I found frames Asana's AI as consumption credits - a lumpy, non-recurring line. Nobody reads API enum values. If the market had priced a seat-licensed AI upsell with an undisclosed top tier, the multiple would not still embed the 'AI replaces seats' frame, the average price target would not sit 10% below spot, and the 25-delta skew would not be paying 6.6 vol points for downside into the exact call where the number gets disclosed.
findings.independence: Same product surface, so treat as one cluster with the API doc: Asana shipped division-level AI Studio credit allocations with admin soft limits on 2026-06-16 (https://forum.asana.com/t/new-ai-studio-department-level-credit-allocations/1144886) and the Usage API on 2026-07-02 (https://forum.asana.com/t/new-ai-studio-usage-api/1147044) - governance features you only build when large accounts are already blowing through entitlements. Genuinely independent: on the Q1 call management said 'AI product bookings represented 17% of net-new annual recurring revenue, exceeding the full-year 15% target pace' (https://www.fool.com/earnings/call-transcripts/2026/05/28/asana-asan-q1-2027-earnings-transcript/).

findings.finding: Asana retired 7,368,000 shares for $44.985 million in the single quarter ended 2026-04-30 - roughly 3% of shares outstanding in three months at an average of about $6.11 - leaving $154.5 million authorised, against a float already shrunk by Moskovitz's ~27% stake and short interest above 22%.
findings.why_not_priced: It sits in an equity footnote of a 10-Q for a $2.4bn company with 2 published quarterly estimates; no preview I found mentions the pace or the $44.985m figure. If it were priced, previews would be modelling a shrinking share count into the EPS line and the put/call open interest ratio of 0.31 would not coexist with 22%+ of the float short - a company buying 3% of itself a quarter is the other side of that short base.
findings.independence: Different source, same direction on float mechanics: an 2026-08-13 piece attributes the recent rally specifically to short covering and puts short interest above 22% of float (https://www.tipranks.com/news/catalyst/asana-stock-surges-back-in-powerful-short-covering-rally). Note this shares a directional theme with finding 5 but rests on a different document.

findings.finding: monday.com's Q2 print on 2026-08-10 - the first category datapoint issued after Asana last spoke, covering a quarter that overlaps two thirds of Asana's - reported NDR of 109%, 'gross retention is also at historical highs' and 'we are still seeing a double-digit seat growth year-over-year in enterprise', directly contradicting the seat-destruction frame that caps Asana's multiple.
findings.why_not_priced: MNDY fell about 8% on its own print, so the market's takeaway from that day was 'cautious guidance', and the retention detail was consumed as an MNDY fact rather than an Asana read-through. Contemporaneous coverage attributes Asana's August move to short covering, easing inflation and sector rotation 'rather than a reaction to fresh company news' - i.e. the peer's retention data was explicitly not what re-rated ASAN. If it had been priced as a read-through, the skew would not still be paying up for downside on retention.
findings.independence: Asana's own Q1 call said in-quarter NRR 'improved for the fourth consecutive quarter to 97%' and that 'the primary driver of NRR outperformance is seat expansion, not simply lower churn', while the H2 guide assumes 'only modest improvement in our net retention rates' - a conservatively set bar (https://www.fool.com/earnings/call-transcripts/2026/05/28/asana-asan-q1-2027-earnings-transcript/). That is a different company's document from the MNDY transcript, but it is the same transcript I cite in finding 1's independence, so collapse those two to one residual.

findings.finding: Asana enters this print with no dedicated chief accounting officer: CAO/PAO Veronica Sosa resigned on 2026-07-13 effective 2026-08-07, and on 2026-08-26 - six days before the print - the board handed the principal accounting officer role to CFO Aziz Megji, himself appointed only in March 2026 after CFO Sonalee Parekh resigned in February 2026, making three finance-leadership changes in six months.
findings.why_not_priced: The 2026-07-13 resignation got thin aggregator coverage and the 2026-08-26 consolidation of PAO into the CFO seat got essentially none - the stock rose 9% in the five sessions that straddled it. If it were priced, that consolidation would have appeared in the previews as a guidance-quality caveat rather than being absent from all of them, and the run-up into the print would not have been positive. It matters most as tail risk on the reliability of the first-ever full-year AI contribution outlook, delivered by a CFO on his second guide who is also now his own accounting officer.
findings.independence: None that is genuinely independent - the July resignation 8-K (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1477720/000162828026048674/asan-20260713.htm) and the February CFO-resignation disclosure are all the company's own filings, one source cluster. Scored as a single residual.

findings.finding: After a 16.8% twenty-day run-up that contemporaneous coverage attributes to short covering and sector rotation rather than company news, ASAN trades roughly 10% ABOVE the 15-analyst average price target of $9.27 with a consensus 'Hold', and consensus FY27 revenue of $860.8m sits dead centre of the company's own $855.5-863.5m guide - so there is no estimate slack to beat into.
findings.why_not_priced: The baseline already carries the run-up and the +6.6 skew, so I am only claiming the incremental fact: the sell-side target sits below spot and consensus is pinned to the midpoint of the guide, which means an in-line quarter has no room to be rewarded and only the not-yet-modelled AI outlook can be. I have sized this as a partial overlap with the baseline rather than a fresh finding, which is why it is under one point.
findings.independence: https://www.tipranks.com/news/catalyst/asana-stock-surges-back-in-powerful-short-covering-rally (2026-08-13) independently characterises the August move as 'a technical rebound and short-covering rally rather than a reaction to fresh company news' with >22% of float short. Shares the short-interest fact with finding 2 but points the opposite way there, which is deliberate: high short interest raises the bar and supplies squeeze fuel at the same time.

searched_and_found_nothing: Moskovitz insider activity: his last open-market purchase was 2025-08-21 under a 10b5-1 plan adopted 2024-09-05 and he has 71 buys / 0 sells lifetime - the bid has been absent for four prints already, so nothing new here (https://www.secform4.com/insider-trading/1549917.htm)
Recent Form 4 / Rule 144 activity (CEO Rogers sold 1,655 shares 2026-08-27, director Norrington 144 for 61,623 shares 2026-08-20) - all routine 10b5-1 and de minimis relative to float

Asana's free-plan seat cut from 10 users to 2 - real and still generating forum complaints, but it applies only to accounts created on or after 2025-11-12, three quarters before this print, so it is not a Q2 FY27 event
status.asana.com incident history - could not retrieve a dated incident list; the only incident I could confirm (2026-08-31) was resolved the same day per a customer IT notice

web.archive.org snapshot of asana.com/pricing from 2026-05-15 to diff the AI credit allocations against today - the domain is blocked in this environment, so I could not date the credit-entitlement change
Independent price confirmation for the ai_studio_max tier in any reseller, Vendr or public-procurement price list - none exists, so the tier's existence rests on the API enum alone

Layoffs, WARN filings or headcount reduction at Asana - none found; the careers page carries 118 open roles including 15+ AI roles and 23 GTM roles (https://asana.com/jobs/all), but I have no dated prior count to measure the trend against

FedRAMP Moderate authorisation for Asana Gov on 2026-06-24 (https://investors.asana.com/news-releases/news-release-details/asana-achieves-fedrampr-moderate-authorization-asana-gov) - press-released and aggregator-covered, and contributes no revenue in the FY27 guide, so I dropped it rather than pad the set

Takeover / activist angle - two 2026 listicles name Asana as a takeover candidate but there is no filing, 13D, or reported process; Moskovitz's super-voting stake makes it structurally unlikely and nothing has changed on it
Post-quarter CEO commentary: Rogers gave a 2026-07-31 interview to diginomica with zero quantitative or forward-looking content

Two search results that looked like fresh catalysts and were not: a 'shares up 8.9%' piece dated 2026/08/29 in its URL that is actually about Q2 FY2026 ($196.9m revenue, September 2025), and a 2026-09-01 preview quoting $193.0m / $0.05 consensus, which are last year's figures - neither used
baseline_tension: Cuts against the baseline: the skew pays 6.6 vol points for downside and the sell-side target sits below spot, yet the primary-source evidence I found - AI Studio now licensed per seat with an undisclosed top tier, division-level credit governance shipped mid-quarter, 3% of shares retired in one quarter, and a peer reporting record gross retention with double-digit enterprise seat growth after Asana last spoke - points the other way, which is why I am modestly positive rather than agreeing with the paid-for downside.
